items.explanation: The final expression is y*2; y is 4, so the returned value is 8.

items.explanation: The accumulator is 1²+2²+3²+4² = 30 after four iterations.

items.explanation: The loop computes 1×2×3 = 6, the factorial of three.

items.stem: Arrange the statements to assign a vector to x, copy it to y, square y and display the result. A: y <- x; B: x <- c(1, -1, 3.5, 2); C: [1] 1.00 1.00 12.25 4.00; D: y^2
items.explanation: Create x first, copy it to y, evaluate y^2, then the console displays the four squared values.

items.stem: Arrange the statements to create x, add 2 element-wise, square the result and display it. A: z <- x+2; B: x <- c(1, 2, 3); C: [1] 9 16 25; D: z^2
items.explanation: x must exist before z is assigned; z^2 is then evaluated and its output follows.

items.stem: Arrange the statements to double a vector and print the doubled values. A: y <- 2*x; B: x <- c(1, 3, 5); C: [1] 2 6 10; D: y
items.explanation: Define x, assign the doubled vector to y, evaluate y, and then read the printed output.

items.stem: Arrange the statements to calculate and display the sum of 1, 2, 3 and 4. A: s <- sum(x); B: x <- 1:4; C: [1] 10; D: s
items.explanation: The vector is created before its sum is assigned; evaluating s prints 10.

items.stem: Arrange the statements to take square roots and display the result. A: z <- sqrt(x); B: x <- c(1, 4, 9); C: [1] 1 2 3; D: z
items.explanation: Create x, compute its element-wise square roots, evaluate z, then the output appears.

items.stem: Arrange the statements to square each entry of x and display y. A: y <- x^2; B: x <- c(2, 3, 4); C: [1] 4 9 16; D: y
items.explanation: Assignment to x precedes y <- x^2; evaluating y produces the displayed vector.

items.stem: Arrange the statements to define a function, set an argument, call the function and display the answer. A: f <- function(x) x+1; B: x <- 4; C: [1] 5; D: f(x)
items.explanation: Define f and x before calling f(x); the returned value 5 is printed after the call.

items.stem: Arrange the statements to sort a vector and display the sorted copy. A: x <- c(3, 1, 2); B: y <- sort(x); C: y; D: [1] 1 2 3
items.explanation: Create x, assign sort(x) to y, evaluate y, and then read the printed sorted vector.

items.stem: Arrange the statements to square a vector, sum the squares and display the scalar. A: x <- c(2, 4, 6); B: y <- x^2; C: [1] 56; D: sum(y)
items.explanation: Create x, compute y, evaluate sum(y), then the console prints 4+16+36 = 56.

items.stem: Arrange the statements to compute the mean of a vector and display it. A: m <- mean(x); B: x <- c(2, 4, 6); C: [1] 4; D: m
items.explanation: Create the vector before computing its mean; evaluating m prints 4.
